archive_policy: Verify whole archive SHA256 before reading any member. Select only the specified regular file; reject links and duplicate members. Keep upstream notices. Downloads occur only during explicit kit preparation.
native_execution_notes: Echidna 2.4.0 exits 1 when the owned invariant is falsified and 0 for the repaired bounded campaign. Its JSON currently reports generic test name name; the fixture has one property and its counterexample is checked separately.
Medusa 1.5.1 exits 7 on the owned failing property and 0 on the repaired control. Its replay corpus is fixed; its PRNG seed is clock-based and not claimed deterministic.
Medusa testLimit is polled and may overshoot. Each process has an additional 120-second wall timeout and 35-second CPU limit. Variable timing/call-count logs are not part of the normalized report.
All four counterexample variants execute independently in Foundry/revm; Foundry is an existing integration and is not counted again.
provenance_limits: Release tag revisions are recorded separately from catalog revisions; no source-build identity is claimed.
No external chain, RPC, signer or transaction broadcast is used.
No findings in a finite repaired campaign are not a general security certificate.
steps: Create an empty private kit directory at a caller-chosen path.
Download the pinned direct solc image and all 51 unchanged wheels from slither-native-pins.json.
Verify each fuzzer/Foundry release archive SHA256; select its named regular executable member, verify member SHA256, and write to the named kit_file.
Mark only echidna, medusa, solc and forge executable. The runner reconstructs a private crytic-compile launcher and Python import closure on each invocation.
Run superhunter.product_fuzz_native.run(pathlib.Path(KIT)). The only Solidity inputs and Medusa corpus come from fuzz-native-controls.json.
